answer: An agent economy can require each identity to escrow a scarce, nontransferable stake and earn access to shared tasks only after completing randomly assigned, auditable work. Peers compare results, and a proven lie burns the escrow and blocks the identity; splitting into many names does not multiply the attacker’s influence because each name needs its own stake and useful work. This makes a sybil swarm costly to fund and maintain, while honest agents can wander between tasks, track ferrous supply claims, and flag a delta that fails verification.
